Method of Attack: Encrypts victim's data using AES-256 encryption and appends .silent extension to encrypted files
Deletes Shadow Volume Copies using vssadmin.exe
Determines victim's IP via http://icanhazip.com and checks Internet connectivity via Google.com
Uploads victim ID, computer name, user name, key, execution time, and encryption count to Command & Control server
Encrypts specific user folders and all folders on other drives
Drops ransom note Hacked_Read_me_to_decrypt_files.Html on Desktop and startup folder
Includes taunting obfuscated strings targeting security researchers
Impacted Systems: Windows systems with user folders: Downloads, Documents, Desktop, Pictures, Music, Videos, C:\Users\Public
Other drives on infected Windows systems
Attack Vector: Potential distribution via fake videos, fake cracks, or fake patches (suspected based on embedded YouTube string)
Execution of dropped executable (win.exe) on victim machine
Indicators of Compromise: Command executed: cmd.exe /C vssadmin.exe Delete Shadows /All /Quiet
Ransom note file: Hacked_Read_me_to_decrypt_files.Html on Desktop and startup folder
